topic: Agentic plan-to-code preflight and adversarial certification: executable acceptance criteria, simulation, negative-space review, evidence gates, human override, and regression traceability
research_questions: How do mature agentic engineering and safety systems turn plans into executable preflight checks, scenario simulations, and adversarial certification?
Which acceptance-criteria, negative-space, evidence-gate, human-override, and regression-traceability patterns are documented by primary sources?
How should a plan-to-code gate expose blocked, uncertain, overridden, and certified outcomes without conflating them?
What evidence is necessary to claim that a plan remains safe and complete as implementation and dependencies change?

sources.title: AI RMF Core
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.material_relevance: Defines a continuous Govern-Map-Measure-Manage lifecycle, documented human oversight, pre-deployment and operational testing, uncertainty-aware measurement, residual-risk management, and go/no-go decisions.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.material_relevance: Applies AI RMF to generative AI across the lifecycle and explicitly foregrounds governance, content provenance, pre-deployment testing, incident disclosure, and uncertainty about unknown or hard-to-evaluate risks.

sources.title: Our updated Preparedness Framework
sources.material_relevance: Documents capability thresholds, safeguards reports, scalable automated evaluations, expert deep dives, residual-risk review, and leadership decisions that can approve deployment, request further evaluation, or require stronger protections.

sources.title: Strengthening our Frontier Safety Framework
sources.material_relevance: Shows thresholded early-warning evaluations, tracked and critical capability levels, systematic risk identification, explicit risk-acceptability determinations, mitigation before thresholds, and safety-case reviews before relevant launches or internal deployments.

sources.title: Inspect: An open-source framework for large language model evaluations
sources.publisher: UK AI Security Institute and Meridian Labs
sources.material_relevance: Provides composable tasks, datasets, agents, tools, solvers, and scorers; tool-call approval; sandboxing for untrusted code; parallel and early-stopping runs; and transcript/log analysis for agentic evaluations.

sources.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
sources.material_relevance: Introduces an extensible dynamic environment with realistic tool-using tasks, security test cases, adaptive attacks, and defenses for evaluating agents on untrusted external data.

sources.title: Example autonomy evaluation protocol
sources.material_relevance: Specifies dev/test task separation, elicitation, repeated runs, confidence intervals, transcript and infrastructure checks, aggregation, threshold-to-mitigation mapping, and explicit limitations of evaluation coverage.

sources.title: SWE-bench Verified
sources.material_relevance: Demonstrates human validation of issue descriptions, test patches, and solvability, while preserving a reproducible coding-agent evaluation setup and configuration/version disclosure.

sources.title: System Engineering Handbook: Appendix
sources.material_relevance: Defines verification versus validation, requirements flowdown and bidirectional traceability, simulation/test fixtures, verification methods, certification processes, certification packages, and change authority.

sources.title: SWE-194 - Delivery Requirements Verification
sources.material_relevance: Requires traceability from requirements to tests and results, nominal/off-nominal and boundary testing, regression testing, and documented disposition of unresolved defects or accepted risks.

findings.claim: Mature assurance systems treat a plan-to-code decision as a lifecycle loop rather than a one-time green check.
findings.notes: NIST connects context mapping to measurement and management, requires monitoring and periodic review, and documents that contexts, capabilities, risks, and impacts evolve. NASA places verification, validation, and requirements change control across the system lifecycle.

findings.claim: Executable acceptance criteria need an explicit evidence contract that maps each requirement to a verification method, result, and decision authority.
findings.notes: NASA requires requirements flowdown, bidirectional traceability, verification methods, results, certification products, and change authority. NIST requires formalized measurement and documentation sufficient to inform management decisions.

findings.claim: Adversarial certification must exercise the agent in a dynamic environment with untrusted inputs and adaptive attacks, not only replay a static happy-path test set.
findings.notes: AgentDojo explicitly models evolving attacks and defenses in an extensible dynamic environment. Inspect supports tools, sandboxes, approvals, and agent transcripts. METR warns that task implementations, infrastructure, elicitation, and coverage can invalidate apparently meaningful results.

findings.claim: Negative-space review should include boundary, off-nominal, failure, misuse, and recovery scenarios as first-class acceptance evidence.
findings.notes: NASA calls for nominal, off-nominal, boundary, regression, and hazard-mitigation testing. AgentDojo shows why external data and prompt-injection cases must be represented in the environment.

findings.claim: A single observed pass or fail is insufficient when agent performance is stochastic or capability can be elicited by different scaffolding.
findings.notes: METR requires repeated runs, confidence intervals, and checks for high variance. OpenAI describes evaluations as a lower bound because prompting, fine-tuning, longer rollouts, and novel scaffolding can elicit behavior beyond observed tests.

findings.claim: Thresholds are most useful when they trigger named operational actions and a review path, rather than being presented as an unexplained score.
findings.notes: OpenAI maps capability levels to safeguards, further evaluation, or leadership approval. Google DeepMind uses early-warning and critical capability levels with mitigation and safety-case reviews. METR describes mapping scores to mitigation requirements.

findings.claim: Human override is a controlled exception and review mechanism; it is not equivalent to successful automated verification.
findings.notes: NIST requires documented human oversight, Inspect exposes tool-call approval, and NASA assigns change authority and certification responsibilities. The separation between an override and a verified pass is a direct design inference from those controls.

findings.claim: A certification claim must carry provenance and change-sensitive traceability for the plan, implementation, dependencies, test configuration, and evidence artifacts.
findings.notes: NIST foregrounds provenance and lifecycle evidence; NASA requires traceability and impact analysis for changes; SWE-bench demonstrates that test patches, task definitions, and evaluation configuration materially affect interpretability.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Continuous Govern-Map-Measure-Manage loop with documented context, human oversight, uncertainty, residual risk, and go/no-go decisions.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: A plan-to-code gate should re-evaluate context and risk when the plan, implementation, deployment setting, or dependencies change, and should preserve the evidence supporting each decision.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Risk capability thresholds are coupled to operational commitments, safeguard reports, residual-risk review, and named approval authority.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: A gate should expose threshold crossings together with the required action, reviewer, evidence package, and re-evaluation trigger.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Composable evaluation primitives separate tasks, datasets, agents, tools, solvers, scorers, approvals, sandboxes, execution controls, and analysis.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Acceptance criteria should be represented as composable executable checks whose inputs, tool permissions, scoring rules, and transcript evidence can be independently inspected and reused.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Dynamic scenario environments combine realistic tasks with untrusted data, security cases, adaptive attacks, and defenses.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: The certification corpus should evolve with threat models and include attacks that can change the environment or task state, not only fixed expected-output cases.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Evaluation protocols separate development and held-out testing, repeat runs, inspect transcripts and infrastructure, quantify uncertainty, and map results to mitigations.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: A gate should record task-set identity, run count, variance or confidence interval, elicitation/scaffolding configuration, transcript review, and the action associated with each threshold.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Human validation of task descriptions, test patches, and solvability is used to make coding-agent results interpretable.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Before using an automated acceptance test as a release gate, validate that the test is correct, the requirement is clear, and the scenario is solvable under the declared environment.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Systems engineering uses requirements flowdown, bidirectional traceability, explicit verification and validation methods, simulation, certification packages, and authorized change control.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Plan-to-code evidence should be a traceable certification package, not merely a test summary, and every approved change should carry impact analysis and re-verification scope.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Delivery verification explicitly covers off-nominal, boundary, hazard, regression, traceability, and disposition of accepted residual defects.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: The gate should require negative-space and regression evidence and should make residual risk visible instead of silently treating a documented exception as a pass.

failure_modes.failure_mode: A binary green status is retained after the plan, deployment context, implementation, or dependencies materially change.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Bind evidence to versioned plan, code, configuration, dependency, and environment identities; invalidate or re-scope affected claims after changes and require impact analysis.

failure_modes.failure_mode: One stochastic agent run is treated as a stable estimate of capability or safety.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Require repeated runs, confidence intervals or an explicit uncertainty disposition, and preserve the run configuration and sampling/scaffolding details.

failure_modes.failure_mode: An evaluation failure is caused by a task, scorer, infrastructure, or scaffolding defect but is misclassified as an agent failure.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Add evaluator-health checks, human validation of tasks and expected tests, transcript review for non-maximal runs, and an explicit evaluator-error state.

failure_modes.failure_mode: Untrusted tool output or external content hijacks an agent into violating the intended plan or security property.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Run dynamic prompt-injection and tool-misuse scenarios in sandboxes, use least-privilege approvals, and score both task success and security-property preservation.

failure_modes.failure_mode: Capability is underestimated because the tested scaffold or prompting did not elicit behavior reachable under plausible alternate scaffolds.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Declare elicitation scope, test meaningful alternate scaffolds, record lower-bound limitations, and route material uncertainty to further evaluation rather than certification.

failure_modes.failure_mode: A requirement, test, code change, or residual defect becomes orphaned from the traceability record.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Enforce bidirectional requirement-to-design/code/test/result links, detect orphans, and keep change-impact and regression artifacts in the same certification record.

failure_modes.failure_mode: A human exception or approval is displayed as if it were an automated certification.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Keep override metadata separate from verification results: authority, rationale, scope, residual risk, expiry, compensating controls, and revalidation trigger must be visible.

failure_modes.failure_mode: A static benchmark or known task corpus misses newly relevant attacks, scenarios, or dependency interactions.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Maintain a versioned scenario registry with dynamic/adversarial additions, periodic threat-model review, and a visible coverage-gap or unknown-risk state.

implications.implication: Compile each acceptance criterion into an executable check with an expected evidence type, evaluator version, pass rule, and trace link back to the plan atom.
implications.rationale: This combines NIST’s documented measurement/governance loop, NASA’s requirement verification matrix, and Inspect’s composable evaluation primitives into a plan-to-code evidence contract.

implications.implication: Run a scenario portfolio containing nominal, boundary, off-nominal, recovery, adversarial, human-misuse, and dependency-change cases in isolated environments.
implications.rationale: NASA explicitly calls for boundary, off-nominal, hazard, and regression coverage; AgentDojo and Inspect show how to execute tool-using agents against untrusted or sandboxed environments.

implications.implication: Expose gate outcomes as distinct states: blocked for a hard failed or missing prerequisite, uncertain for insufficient or noisy evidence, overridden for an authorized exception, and certified only for a complete passing evidence package.
implications.rationale: The sources show threshold-triggered actions, safety-case review, uncertainty checks, and authorized certification; the four-state vocabulary is a proposed product representation that keeps those decisions non-equivalent.

implications.implication: Make an override an expiring, auditable exception containing authority, rationale, scope, compensating controls, residual risk, and a revalidation trigger; never rewrite the underlying failed evidence as a pass.
implications.rationale: Documented human oversight, tool-call approval, change authority, waivers, and certification responsibilities support an explicit exception record rather than status conflation.

implications.implication: Require a certification bundle containing plan/spec identity, implementation and dependency identities, environment and evaluator versions, scenario-set identity, transcripts/logs, repeated-run statistics, traceability links, reviewer identity, and residual-risk disposition.
implications.rationale: The combined provenance, certification-package, uncertainty, and evaluation-log patterns are the minimum evidence needed for a later reviewer to reproduce or challenge the claim.

implications.implication: Add automatic impact analysis and selective re-verification when any traced requirement, code path, dependency, tool permission, evaluator, or scenario definition changes.
implications.rationale: NASA requires impact assessment and updated traceability for changes, while NIST treats risk management as continuous across the lifecycle and component value chain.

implications.implication: Separate evaluator-health failures from system-under-test failures and require human review of ambiguous or non-maximal runs before assigning a gate state.
implications.rationale: METR calls for transcript and infrastructure checks; SWE-bench validates task/test quality; Inspect provides log and transcript analysis primitives.

implications.implication: Treat coverage gaps and unknown risks as first-class evidence outcomes, and refresh the scenario registry through adversarial findings, incidents, dependency changes, and external threat-model updates.
implications.rationale: NIST notes unknown and difficult-to-evaluate risks; AgentDojo models evolving attacks; Google DeepMind describes framework updates and tracked levels as new evidence emerges.

novel_ideas.idea: Evidence-state lattice with non-conflating transitions: blocked, uncertain, overridden, and certified are separate nodes, with explicit allowed transitions and no direct override-to-certified shortcut.
novel_ideas.rationale: Thresholded action paths, uncertainty checks, and authorized certification suggest a state model that preserves why a decision was made and prevents an exception from erasing failed evidence.

novel_ideas.idea: Evidence invalidation graph: every evidence item declares the plan, code, dependency, environment, evaluator, and scenario identities it covers; changes invalidate only the reachable claims and trigger targeted re-verification.
novel_ideas.rationale: This operationalizes bidirectional traceability, configuration/change control, provenance, and lifecycle monitoring as a dependency-aware evidence graph.

novel_ideas.idea: Negative-space matrix generated from each acceptance criterion: pair the positive assertion with boundary, omission, misuse, adversarial-input, partial-completion, timeout, recovery, and dependency-failure cases.
novel_ideas.rationale: NASA’s off-nominal and boundary guidance plus AgentDojo’s attack/task pairing provide a basis for making negative space mechanically visible rather than relying on reviewer intuition.

novel_ideas.idea: Override lease: an override carries a time or change-bound expiry and automatically returns the gate to uncertain or blocked when its compensating evidence is stale.
novel_ideas.rationale: Continuous monitoring, authorized change control, and reassessment when new evidence emerges support treating exceptions as bounded temporal decisions rather than permanent passes.

novel_ideas.idea: Confidence-aware certification: require a minimum repeated-run confidence target for high-risk criteria and display the confidence interval alongside the state, not hidden inside a score.
novel_ideas.rationale: METR explicitly uses repeated runs and confidence intervals, while OpenAI describes measured evaluations as lower bounds; exposing uncertainty makes the certification claim proportionate to the evidence.

unresolved_questions.question: What exact acceptance criteria and risk classes require independent or external review rather than only an internal automated gate?
What repeated-run count, confidence target, and uncertainty disposition are appropriate for each plan risk class and scenario type?
Which changes to plans, code, dependencies, tools, environments, or evaluators should invalidate all evidence versus only a reachable subset of claims?
Who may authorize an override, what residual-risk ceiling applies, and when must the exception expire or be re-approved?
What threat-model coverage and dynamic scenario refresh cadence are sufficient to claim that negative-space review remains current?
